seal_chamber.name: The Seal Chamber
seal_chamber.description: The sealed site itself, the reason the academy exists. Only the Warden enters, and the way in is watched. Contents differ by academy: a monster at Myrdath, a tomb at Veyra, an elixir at Ashvale, a crack at Halvard. Most students never see the door. Halvard: the corridor toward it runs colder, the lanterns burn unnaturally steady, and students who wander close feel pressure on their ears and turn back before the door.
seal_chamber.access: Forbidden — the Warden only; magic near it is banned

wardens_office.name: The Warden's Office
wardens_office.description: A working room adjoining the site, not the academy, on Floor 1 down its own corridor, holding the only stair to the Seal Chamber. Mana consumption ledgers and the seal's condition are recorded here, and only the Warden can read them. Students have no reason to come; staff come only when summoned. Halvard: the Acting Warden refuses the Royal Inspectorate every time. The wall it shares with the site is always cold.
wardens_office.vibe: an ashtray never emptied, old paper, one lamp.

arbiter_hall.name: The Arbiter Hall
arbiter_hall.description: The great hall, home to the Arbiter Stone. Entrance Event sorting once a year, general assembly the rest: announcements, Results and Dorm Ranking, Graduation. Students sit before the Stone constantly and touch it exactly once in their lives. The Stone is warm to the touch, warmer than it should be.

ring_dining_hall.name: The Ring Dining Hall
ring_dining_hall.description: Formal hall, tables in a ring around an open floor so all four dorms face each other across empty space. Musicians in the gallery, an illusion sky that turns a whole day's weather overhead, climate runes holding it windless and warm. Used only for the Entrance Feast and other full-academy meals. Empty most of the year and unsettling to walk alone.

portrait_hall.name: Portrait Hall
portrait_hall.description: A long corridor of past headmasters, past wardens, and each year's competition champions. Winning at any tier puts your face on the wall; losing means the wall skips your year. Halvard: the previous Warden's portrait (name unknown) hangs with a black ribbon, and every student slows in front of it.

founders_statue_and_park.name: Founder's Statue and Park
founders_statue_and_park.description:
Open parkland with lawns, paths and benches; the main green space on campus and the nicest place to be outdoors between classes. Picnic blankets dot the lawns on any fair day, and weathered wooden picnic tables stand in the shade along the paths. Everyday use: sitting and talking, lunch on a blanket or at a picnic table, reading, napping, jogging the paths, couples finding somewhere semi-private. Busiest at lunch and on warm afternoons. On a fair day, an hour on the grass restores more than an hour anywhere indoors.
The Founder's Statue stands at its centre: bronze, the academy's founding warden, cold even in full sun, its outstretched hand polished bright by the Founder's Hand superstition, with a queue that snakes across the lawn on exam mornings. Focus of Academy Founder Day in Month 9.
Home of the Faraway Laugh story.

lore.title: The Founder's Hand
lore.summary: Rule: touch the Founder's Statue's outstretched hand before an exam, always the hand, always on the way out.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Faraway Laugh
lore.summary: Where: Founder's Park and the tree-lined paths, after dark.

seasons.Spring: The first warm day fills every lawn.
seasons.Summer: Busiest of all: picnic blankets from lunch to dusk.
seasons.Autumn: Leaf piles along the paths, and the benches move into the last sun.
seasons.Winter: The benches stand empty, snowmen appear on the lawns overnight, and the exam-morning queue to the Founder's Hand stamps a path through the snow.

bell_tower.name: Bell Tower
bell_tower.description:
Marks class periods, meals, and curfew. Its pattern changes during The Thinning. The seven o'clock bell wakes the mana lanterns; the eight o'clock bell begins curfew. After it the lanterns drop to their night burn, each dormitory seals to its own students, and staff walk the courtyards for the first hour. Birds leave the roof just before it sounds. A bell-keeper looks after the bells and their ropes, and takes on a student for a paid shift now and then.
Home of the Thirteenth Stroke story.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Thirteenth Stroke
lore.summary: Where: anywhere outdoors after the eight o'clock bell.

lecture_halls.name: Lecture Halls
lecture_halls.description: Tiered rooms holding all four dorms at once, for the shared track: Magic Theory, History, Etiquette, Creature Studies. Each year level has its own floor: first-years on Floor 2, second-years on Floor 3, third-years on Floor 4. The only classrooms where students sit beside other types. Each class leaves its traces: chalk diagrams, old maps, polished desks, mud and straw after Creature Studies.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Long Corridor
lore.summary: Where: the castle's main corridor, walked alone after the night burn.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Night Student
lore.summary: Where: the Lecture Hall tier, after curfew.

seminar_rooms.name: Seminar Rooms
seminar_rooms.description: On Floor 3, beside the second-year Lecture Halls; first-years climb up to them, third-years come down. Smaller rooms for dorm-specific teaching and discussion. Four of most things, since Combat, Potion Crafting and Dark Magic Defense are taught to each dorm separately. Small enough that a badly cast spell fills the whole room. Chalk circles ghost the floors.

potion_halls.name: Potion Halls
potion_halls.description: Four brewing halls on Floor 4, one per dorm at the base of each of four towers, each equipped differently because each type approaches the craft differently, doubling as ventilated laboratories. Disposal rules are strict. The line between legitimate Potion Crafting and forbidden poison magic is drawn here and watched closely. Four towers vent four colours of steam over the roofline.
potion_halls.vibe: coloured steam, bubbling vats, warning labels.

combat_grounds.name: Combat Grounds
combat_grounds.description: Four separate training areas so the dorms train apart, kept well away from buildings. Cross-dorm sparring only during Training Week, with the Magic Duelling Club as the standing exception. Spent mana makes the air shiver at dusk. At the far corner of the grounds, three minutes' walk from the rings, stands the Sparring Pavilion, the one building the four training areas share: equipment store, rest area, and the Magic Duelling Club's headquarters.
combat_grounds.access: Dorm-separated training areas; duels only inside a warded ring

faculty_offices.name: Faculty Offices
faculty_offices.description: Records, consultations, and grade arguments. Every teacher runs a club, so half of these double as club offices. Students can often guess who was just there from what they left behind: marked essays, borrowed books, half-finished cups, unsigned club forms.
faculty_offices.vibe: doors ajar, cluttered desks, busy corridor.

staff_room.name: Staff Room
staff_room.description: Teachers' territory; students knock and wait outside. What is said here about the ranking, the students and the Warden does not leave the room. Warded so heavily that no sound crosses the threshold.

workshop.name: Workshop
workshop.description: Down in the castle's vaulted undercroft beneath the Lecture Halls, where thick stone keeps its noise off the classrooms above and flues carry forge smoke up through the walls. Crafting space for the Smithing, Tailoring and Brewing clubs, plus Creation practicals and equipment repair. Tools, forges, benches. Enchantment sparks hang in the air after the hammer stops. Its lathes and tool racks are Caelmari-made.

main_library.name: Main Library
main_library.description: Reading rooms and general collections; the academy's working heart in exam weeks. Open to all four dorms, one of the few places students mix by choice rather than schedule. The upper shelves sit permanently in shadow and are a standard hiding place for students avoiding class. In exam weeks, Firetooth tins and Star Cookies cover the study tables. A battered book of world myths (the Holy Grail, the Four Who Saved the World) is the most borrowed title in a first-year's first month.

lore.title: Sleeping in the Library
lore.summary: Story: fall asleep over a book and you wake somewhere else: a reading room with the wrong number of doors, shelves out of order, nobody else in the building.

restricted_section.name: Restricted Section
restricted_section.description: Below the Archive, the deepest room of the Library. Texts on the twenty forbidden arts, the only place the crimes are written down in detail. Access controlled; being caught inside without permission is serious. Students report the sense of being counted.
restricted_section.access: Restricted — permission required; being caught inside is serious

archive.name: Archive
archive.description: Beneath the Library, reached by a stair behind the reading rooms. Academy records going back centuries: enrollment, sorting, exam marks, dorm rankings, competition brackets. Dry, exhaustive, and the only honest account of how each dorm has actually performed.

study_rooms.name: Study Rooms
study_rooms.description: Small bookable rooms, impossible to reserve before exam weeks. Fights over booking slots are permanent academy life. Soundproofed; late-night groups bring Nightwell's Vigil or Firetooth.

common_rooms.name: Common Rooms
common_rooms.description: One per dorm, for study, arguments, and Dorm Day displays when the dormitory opens to visitors. Theirs alone the rest of the year. Free kettle and tea, against the mall's paid cafés. Every room has one good chair that unofficially belongs to someone, and a preservation locker beside the kettle where food from home is kept and shared.

lore.title: Dragonchess
lore.summary: Play: starts as ordinary chess (drawn from chess and shogi) on floating checkered spheres over golden clockwork pedestals that materialise the pieces.

seasons.Summer: Windows open, and the arguments carry outside.
seasons.Winter: Everyone crowds the heaters and the kettle never cools.

canteen.name: Canteen
canteen.description: A single canteen for all four dorms on the castle's ground floor, just off the Main Courtyard. Everyday eating, free, open at set hours. Casual and noisy, unlike the Ring Dining Hall, and where most social life happens for students who cannot afford the mall. Loudest at five past noon. The default when points are tight; lunch crowds sort by friendship more than dorm. The main kitchen lies behind the Canteen, supplying its daily meals and preparing the Ring Dining Hall's feasts on major occasions. A dedicated section with its own benches, ovens and ingredient cupboard serves as the Cooking Club's regular venue.

lore.title: The Lucky Roll
lore.summary: The Canteen's free filled roll, baked in batches, no two fillings alike, nothing written down.

seasons.Winter: Porridge, thick broth and second helpings.

laundry.name: Laundry
laundry.description: One in each dormitory. Uniforms, bedding and linens, self-service and free against the mall's paid service. Students on detention often end up working here. The free rune tubs are slow and hard on fabric, which is why bottom-band uniforms wear out faster. Talk carries over the rune tubs, and half the rumours on campus pass through here.

bathhouse_and_washrooms.name: Bathhouse and Washrooms
bathhouse_and_washrooms.description: One in each dormitory. Regional in character and one of the few genuinely relaxed spaces on campus. Dorm-segregated, and a natural place for conversations that would not happen elsewhere; running water covers talk better than a door. Rune heaters make it the one place on campus that is truly warm. Home of the Third Stall ghost story. A long soak here takes the ache out of anything short of an injury.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Third Stall
lore.summary: Where: one stall in every Bathhouse and Washroom block, always occupied, never answers.

seasons.Winter: The most crowded room in each dorm after dinner.

storage_and_lockers.name: Storage and Lockers
storage_and_lockers.description: Personal storage lining the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor of the castle; in the dorms, students simply keep things in their rooms. Each locker answers only to its owner's bracelet. Since Effigy curses work through a personal belonging, locker security is taken seriously.

mall.name: The Mall
mall.description:
The most popular building on campus and where students spend most free time. Crown-funded, holding everything a student needs without leaving: tailor, barber, laundry service, restaurants, tea houses and cafés, bakery, music rooms, art studios, game halls, and a multipurpose store. Everything costs points, with a basic free version of each available in the dorms. Familiar names: Nightwell, Merryhew's, the Sunfizz counter, the bakery. Ground level is food, tailoring, and supplies. Second floor is private dining, tea shops, and gaming parlors. The top deck belongs to the practice studios and meditation nooks. Its busiest tea house is a Yozakuran chain.
Feel: warm, bright, loud.
Gift shops inside The Mall:
Quillfeather's: a narrow bookseller with a ladder on rails; new books at the front, second-hand at the back.
Pennywhistle Curios: gifts, games and trinkets; the window changes with every festival.
Barrow & Vine: wine, ale, spirits and tobacco. Asks for the bracelet, and reminds students they may drink only on the rest day and in the holidays.
Greenwick's: flowers, pot plants, seeds and fruit, run with the Gardening Club.
The Tinker's Bench: tools, craft and hobby supplies, fishing tackle and beast-care goods.
The Salaffian Oven: a food stall with flatbread straight from the oven and southern spices.
Tailor's Row: clothes, shoes, cologne and tailoring alterations.

lore.title: Sunfizz
lore.summary: The soda every student drinks, sold at the Commissary and the Mall store in heavy glass bottles.

lore.title: Ardenne
lore.summary: The luxury marque in magical equipment: focuses, instruments, cases, measuring tools.

lore.title: Firetooth
lore.summary: A tin of hard sweets hot enough to make the eyes water, sold everywhere.

lore.title: The Oracle Shell
lore.summary: A palm-sized novelty shell sold at Merryhew's, the Mall's joke shop, that answers any spoken question with yes, no, or ask again later.

lore.title: Star Cookie
lore.summary: A star-shaped bakery biscuit.

seasons.Summer: The Sunfizz counter queue reaches the door.
seasons.Winter: The warmest crowded place on campus; nobody hurries out.

club_rooms.name: Club Rooms
club_rooms.description:
Roughly thirty rooms of wildly uneven quality down one long corridor on the castle's Floor 1, opening off the Main Courtyard. Centuries-old clubs hold proper halls; a month-old club with five reluctant members gets a converted storeroom. Allocation is the Student Council's most bitterly contested duty. The Theatre Troupe keeps its own club room for meetings, read-throughs and rehearsals. For performances it uses an old indoor amphitheatre off the same corridor, no longer used for classes or assemblies: semicircular tiers of stone seats facing a sunken floor, with heavy curtains and portable scenery turning one end into a stage. It stands empty between productions; before a show, the corridor fills with costumes, scenery and performers waiting for their cue.
Home of the Applause story.

lore.title: Dragonchess
lore.summary: Play: starts as ordinary chess (drawn from chess and shogi) on floating checkered spheres over golden clockwork pedestals that materialise the pieces.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Applause
lore.summary: Where: the old amphitheatre off the Club Rooms corridor, during a late rehearsal.

student_council_chamber.name: Student Council Chamber
student_council_chamber.description: A small room at the far end of the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, permanently buried in club paperwork. Six seats, president, vice president and one representative per dorm, in a room built for four.

notice_board.name: Notice Board
notice_board.description: A long wall of boards in the castle's Floor 1 entrance hall, at the foot of the main stair, where every student passes on the way to class. Club recruitment, exam results, dorm rankings and competition brackets, posted publicly, alongside the student-run half: tutoring offers, study groups, festival posters, lost-item notes and small warnings. After results it is a crowd with elbows. Paid-work openings go within a day. Unofficial notices, dares and betting slips go up overnight and vanish by dawn. Lost items are listed here before they reach the Lost & Found counter at Reception.

mail_tower.name: Mail Tower
mail_tower.description:
The academy's only regular contact with outside: letters and parcels. The upper floors are the aviary where message birds are kept and flown; Creature Studies uses it for bird handling. A sorting floor below handles parcels, with numbered lockers and a tally token for collection; birds carry letters and light goods, heavy goods come slowly by cart. Sunday is the heaviest sorting day, and students on shifts learn everyone's family news first. Students write home from the desks on the sorting floor; a reply takes about a week, and sometimes a small parcel comes with it.
Feel: feathers, birdcall, cold stairwell.
Before the long breaks the sorting floor overflows with parcels going home.

courtyards.name: Courtyards
courtyards.description: Open spaces between buildings where students can hangout. Not designed for anything in particular, which is exactly why they work. Every flat edge worn smooth from centuries of sitting.
courtyards.vibe: open stone, sunny noon, windy dusk.

seasons.Summer: Students chase the shade around the stone.
seasons.Winter: Swept stone in the middle, snowball fights in the drifts at the edges.

sports_field.name: Sports Field
sports_field.description: Soccer, running, and Sports Day in Month 6. A running track circles the soccer pitch: home ground of the Soccer Club and the Running Club. Magic banned outright in play, so this is the one part of the academy where being a powerful mage counts for nothing.

seasons.Winter: Once the snow settles the field closes; the Soccer and Running Clubs move into the Gymnasium and onto the cleared paths.

gymnasium.name: Gymnasium
gymnasium.description: Home of the Gymnastics and Basketball clubs, and of the Swimming Club, which trains in the outdoor pool beside it. Indoor training, used heavily in bad weather and during The Thinning lockdown, when nobody is permitted outside for a week and the place never goes quiet.

seasons.Winter: It is shared by every club that normally trains outside, and booking slots are fought over.

swimming_pool.name: Swimming Pool
swimming_pool.description:
An outdoor pool beside the Gymnasium, its water kept warm by runes along the rim. Sport clubs and general recreation. Water-type students are banned from competing seriously, which they complain about constantly.
Home of the Night Swimmer story.
swimming_pool.vibe: sun on water, splashing, wet stone.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Night Swimmer
lore.summary: Where: the Swimming Pool after dark, most often in winter when the rune-warmed water steams.

seasons.Summer: Crowded from the last class to the eight o'clock bell.
seasons.Winter: The rune-warmed water steams in the cold; the Swimming Club trains through it and sprints the few steps to the Gymnasium.

archery_range.name: Archery Range
archery_range.description: Open range for the Archery Club. Magic banned in play like all sport clubs, so it comes down to the arm and the eye. One of the quietest places on the grounds.

grassy_field_and_hills.name: Grassy Field and Hills
grassy_field_and_hills.description:
Wide open rolling ground in the far grounds, twenty minutes' walk from the Main Courtyard, used for recreation year-round, with the castle small in the distance. It is big: the Observation Tower stands on its nearer crest, the Old Hut is another ten minutes out on the far slope, and the lake shore and the Forest treeline are each a quarter of an hour away. On Star Night the hills fill with students in tents and bedrolls, and the campus below goes dark for the stars.
Home of the Walking Lantern story.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Walking Lantern
lore.summary: Where: the Grassy Field and Hills, after dark.

seasons.Spring: Kites go up on every windy afternoon.
seasons.Summer: Long evenings on blankets until the eight o'clock bell.
seasons.Autumn: The grass turns gold and the wind picks up.
seasons.Winter: The slopes become sledding runs, on trays borrowed from the Canteen.

forest.name: Forest
forest.description: Wide old woodland at the farthest edge of the grounds, past the far slope of the Hills (a quarter of an hour from the field, twenty-five minutes along the lake shore). Creature Studies fieldwork, foraging, walking, and where students go when they want to not be found. Students leave a bite before eating there (Eating in the Forest superstition). Creature Studies teaches there and patrols watch its edge. A deer path, half an hour's walk, leads deep in to the Forest Clearing and its Elder Oak, the one bright place inside it.
forest.access: Far edge of the grounds; curfew applies after dark

lore.title: Eating in the Forest
lore.summary: Rule: share first.

seasons.Spring: Foraging season opens: wild garlic and early greens at the edges.
seasons.Summer: The canopy closes and the Forest is at its darkest by day.
seasons.Autumn: Mushrooms and nuts; Creature Studies warns about the ones that look alike.
seasons.Winter: Dusk comes early, so the patrols turn students back from the treeline by late afternoon; tracks in the snow show what else walks there.

boathouse_and_lake.name: Boathouse and Lake
boathouse_and_lake.description: Vast open water in the far grounds, twenty minutes' walk beyond the Gardens, for rowing, swimming and the Fishing Club. The boathouse stores the craft and doubles as a quiet place to sit. Three minutes' walk along the shore from the boathouse stands the Fishing Club's Fishing House, with its own dock. Sound carries strangely across the water: a far-bank conversation arrives too clearly. Home of the Crying on the Water story; the boathouse refuses bookings after dark. Willow Island sits in the middle of the lake, reached only by boat.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Crying on the Water
lore.summary: Where: the Lake, after dark.

seasons.Spring: Rowing season opens once the water warms.
seasons.Summer: The lake is at its busiest: rowers, swimmers off the jetty, the Fishing Club at dawn.
seasons.Autumn: Morning mist sits on the water until mid-morning.
seasons.Winter: The boats are stored, ice forms along the shallows, and the boathouse lends a boat only on a still, mild day.

gardens.name: Gardens
gardens.description:
Cultivated grounds tended by students and staff, growing Potion Crafting reagents alongside ordinary plants. The Gardening Club effectively runs them, and students gather here before the Harvest Festival. Everything grows a little too well. Halvard: the Sky outcasts' meeting ground; the far end is a reliable place to skip class.
Home of the Breath on the Glass story.
gardens.vibe: turned earth, herb beds in long rows.

lore.title: Ghost Story - Breath on the Glass
lore.summary: Where: inside the Gardens' greenhouses, in the late afternoon and evening.

seasons.Spring: Planting season: seedling rows under glass cloches.
seasons.Summer: Everything overgrows; the Gardening Club weeds daily.
seasons.Autumn: The harvest comes in for the Harvest Festival.
seasons.Winter: The beds sleep under straw and snow; the reagents grow on in the greenhouses, which glow warm through the dark afternoons.

menagerie.name: Menagerie
menagerie.description:
Live specimens for Creature Studies, housed and handled by students under supervision. Beast Handling Club territory. Halvard: the Creature Studies teacher lives beside it in converted stables. Mucking out is the highest-paying paid-work post because nobody volunteers. The animals sense weather changes before the handlers. Magical Beast lives here.
Home of the When the Pens Go Quiet story.

lore.title: Ghost Story - When the Pens Go Quiet
lore.summary: Where: the Menagerie, from dusk into the night.

seasons.Spring: Young ones are born and the handlers barely sleep.
seasons.Winter: The animals grow thick coats, the pens are strawed deep, and the smaller specimens sleep through the cold in heated boxes.

observation_tower.name: Observation Tower
observation_tower.description: A high tower on the nearer crest of the Hills, five minutes up from the field, for astral and celestial work, most important to Mystic students; the Divination Society meets here. The most contested spot on campus on Star Night. Instruments turn by themselves at night. Its great telescope has a Norvaine starglass lens, the Divination Society's pride.

seasons.Summer: Short nights; the Divination Society waits for midnight.
seasons.Winter: Winter nights are the clearest and the coldest; the Divination Society works in coats and gloves.

medical_centre.name: Medical Centre
medical_centre.description:
A white-walled building of its own, four minutes' walk from the Mall, with a herb garden along one side: more than an infirmary, less than a hospital. Treatment rooms, a small apothecary, and an inpatient ward where students stay overnight or for days under care. Staffed by Spiritual mages; busiest after Practical Magic, in competition weeks, exam weeks, and after The Thinning. Nurses see injuries they must report, and injuries they leave off the report. The attached Healing Ward is a teaching space where students practise on real patients under supervision. Staff can spot a Nightwell's Vigil overdose at a glance. Can heal any minor to mid injury to pristine; anything beyond is stabilised here and sent on to a proper hospital. The ward's beds are for the injured first, but a nurse will let an exhausted student lie down for an hour.
Home of the Last Bed story.
medical_centre.vibe: white walls, clean linen, too quiet.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Last Bed
lore.summary: Where: the Medical Centre, at night, for students kept in overnight.

seasons.Winter: The winter cold that goes round campus fills its ward with head colds.

commissary.name: Commissary
commissary.description: The academy shop, a big open-sided stall of its own, three minutes' walk from the Mall: one broad roof on timber posts, open on all four sides, its counters and shelves crammed to the rafters like a general store that sells a bit of everything. Supplies, uniforms, stationery, reagents, equipment, with special orders for anything not stocked. The cheap tier against the mall's store; specialised items can still eat a week of points. Sunfizz sells here for eight points, bottles returned for two. Everyday kit: notebooks, pencils, pen nibs and ink, folders, satchels, printed class textbooks; reagents and equipment on the back shelves. Its cheap stationery and everyday kit are Caelmari-made.

lore.title: Sunfizz
lore.summary: The soda every student drinks, sold at the Commissary and the Mall store in heavy glass bottles.

lore.title: Firetooth
lore.summary: A tin of hard sweets hot enough to make the eyes water, sold everywhere.

reception_and_gatehouse.name: Reception and Gatehouse
reception_and_gatehouse.description: Where visitors are received and logged, and the formal boundary of the academy. Everyone entering or leaving passes through, which makes it the most watched building on campus. The boundary wards are felt as a change of pressure in the gateway. The Gatehouse includes a visiting parlour where students meet family and approved visitors during visiting hours, with worn armchairs, a tea table and windows facing the approach road. Visitors are logged at Reception before entering; meeting here does not give them access to the rest of the grounds.
reception_and_gatehouse.access: The only way in or out

groundskeepers_lodge.name: Groundskeeper's Lodge
groundskeepers_lodge.description: Small quarters at the edge of the grounds for staff who maintain the fields, gardens and walls. The Groundskeeping club reports here. The one building on campus where nothing is enchanted.

seasons.Winter: Groundskeeping clears the paths of snow before the seven o'clock bell.

detention_tower.name: Detention Tower
detention_tower.description: One of the castle core's towers, climbed by its own narrow spiral stair from Floor 1. Where punished students are sent after classes for menial work: copying, cleaning, sorting archive material. The academy's only visible enforcement, and a mild one, which raises the question of what happens to students who do something genuinely serious.

meditation_rooms.name: Meditation Rooms
meditation_rooms.description: An old, weathered building built like a riad: blank outer walls with few windows, every room facing inward onto a shaded central courtyard with a still, shallow pool. Moss and vines cover its walls and dense, leafy trees crowd close around it; between the thick walls and the trees, no sound from the campus gets in. Small, dim rooms with floor cushions serve will-focus training, and the courtyard is for anyone who simply needs to sit. Open to every student, for training or just to take a breath. The one house rule: speak no louder than a murmur, and leave others to their silence. Mana settles and refills faster in the silence; students come before exams and after long practicals.
meditation_rooms.vibe: calm, serene, hushed, moss and cool stone.

seasons.Winter: The bare vines let more pale light into the courtyard, and the pool wears a thin skin of ice.

dovecote.name: The Dovecote
dovecote.description: A compound on academy grounds but not of the academy, reporting to the crown; the Headmaster has no authority over anyone inside. Doves are permanent, rotated in from the capital, and not academy staff. They arrest for forbidden magic, investigate incidents, hold prisoners briefly, and send serious cases onward. Always in pure marble-white cloaks. Students call it the Coop or the Roost, and the Doves themselves Pigeons, and fear it regardless; they cross the courtyard in front of it faster than any other. Halvard: a Commander and a Senior Dove second (who also teaches Dark Magic Defense) are tracing an unregistered forbidden-magic group whose traces they have found, knowing nothing of its name, members or aims.

royal_inspectorate.name: The Royal Inspectorate
royal_inspectorate.description: A suite of offices on Castle Floor 1 behind a heavy door hung with the crown's banners: academy stone, crown ground. The Headmaster's authority stops at that door. Its wing is the same Floor 1 wing as the Warden's corridor, which neither side enjoys. A crown office auditing academic standards and mana output, answering to the capital. Where the Doves handle crime, the Inspectorate handles performance: exam results, ranking integrity, and how much the student body actually feeds the seal. That last duty puts them in the Warden's territory, since the Warden keeps the ledgers and the Inspectorate wants to read them. Halvard: they blame the breach on the Warden's office and press the Acting Warden, who refuses every time.
royal_inspectorate.access: Crown office — the Headmaster has no authority past the door

cathedral.name: The Cathedral
cathedral.description: A house of worship for Asmoday, Goddess of Creation, on academy grounds but answerable to its own authority. Services open to all; its clergy are not academy employees and teach that Asmoday created magic and gifted it to mortals. Every service opens with the Shaping of the World; the clergy teach that Asmoday fractured magic after the First Bargain. That a goddess of creation holds ground at an institution built around sealing things away is a tension nobody discusses openly. It also runs orphanages across the kingdom, the Asmoday's Mercy houses. Halvard: run by a steward who keeps the registry of every oath sworn on academy grounds. A service is held every Sunday morning, from nine to eleven, and the pews are open every day for anyone who wants to sit in quiet. Students of every dormitory come: some to pray, some for the singing, some because it is the one place a conversation with a stranger does not seem strange. Mana comes back a little faster in the quiet of the nave; the clergy call it Asmoday's grace, the academy calls it the silence, and both are glad to see students on the pews.

noble_houses_liaison.name: The Noble Houses' Liaison
noble_houses_liaison.description: A small elegant manor hung with the banners of the noble houses, standing near the Cathedral and the Dovecote. A standing office representing the noble houses' interests, and the reason noble conduct is a graded part of Etiquette rather than a courtesy. It tracks promising students long before Graduation in Month 11, keeps its own notes on who is worth approaching, and hosts house representatives. Students who do not catch its attention usually never learn it exists. Its protocol follows Velmoran court manners.

banking_house.name: The Banking House
banking_house.description: A square stone building with a flat roof, heavy double doors, and a gilded coin emblem mounted above the entrance. The academy's only currency exchange, converting points to real money and back at 1:1 either way. It also moves real coin in and out of the grounds: family money, paid-work earnings and betting settlements all become coin here. It stands outside the mall, so a visit is a deliberate errand. A branch of the World Bank of the Arslan Sultanate; its clerks answer to the Sultanate, not the academy.

forest_clearing.name: Forest Clearing
forest_clearing.description: A single oak called the Elder Oak stands in an open clearing in the middle of the Forest, so broad a dozen students holding hands cannot circle it, and older than the castle by anyone's guess. The canopy opens above the clearing, so the oak stands in full sun while the woods around it stay dim; the muffled quiet of the Forest gives way to birdsong at its edge, and gold motes drift in the light even on grey days. Its roots pull the ground's mana into slow currents unlike anywhere else on campus, and a wild field of rare flowers has spread across the clearing around it, in colours found nowhere else. The Gardening Club has tried transplanting them; they wilt within a day of leaving the clearing. A deer path leads in from the treeline, about thirty minutes' walk. Students come to read, nap between the roots, or be alone without feeling lost. The crust for Eating in the Forest goes on its roots. Patrols turn students back at dusk, and nobody answers their name out here after dark. In winter the clearing stays green and in flower while snow lies everywhere around it. Sitting among the oak's roots, a mage feels their mana refill like water finding its level.
forest_clearing.vibe: sunlit, still, majestic, wildflowers and birdsong.

seasons.Spring: The flower field comes in weeks before anything else on campus.

rooftop.name: Rooftop
rooftop.description:
The flat lead roofs of the castle core, joined by parapet walks and short stairs between the gables. Officially out of bounds. The only way up is a small locked door off the Bell Tower stair, and the trick of opening it is passed from older students to younger ones, never written down; being shown the way up means someone has decided you belong. From the parapet the whole academy lies open: the courtyards, the four dormitories, the Hills, the Lake, the Forest's dark edge, the white roofs of the Dovecote. At night the mana lanterns spread below like a lit map, and at month end you can watch them dim together. The campus's quiet romantic secret: couples come up for sunset and the lantern view, and a hidden corner behind the eastern gable is where confessions happen. Nobody who has been brought up here tells, and the rule is to leave a corner free if someone is already in it. Birds lift off just before each bell, and the lead hums underfoot when it rings. Staff walk the courtyards after curfew, never the roof.
Home of the Other Climber story.
rooftop.vibe: wide sky, wind, sun-warm lead, a shared secret.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Other Climber
lore.summary: Where: the Rooftop, at night.

seasons.Summer: Every corner is taken at sunset.
seasons.Winter: The lead roofs ice over and even the couples stay away.

headmasters_office.name: Headmaster's Office
headmasters_office.description: At the end of the Faculty Offices corridor, a round room up a short stair, its tall windows over the Main Courtyard. Forty years of one Elf's tenure fill it: shelves layered deep with books, and letters and small gifts from graduates. In the window stands a sapling grown from the Elder Oak, forty years old and still knee-high. Students come only when it matters: serious discipline, a request to repeat a year, news no one wants to hear. The bench outside is where the real waiting happens. Visitors from the Royal Inspectorate and the Dovecote are received here, since the Headmaster has no authority inside the Dovecote's walls or past the Inspectorate's door. The door stands open whenever the Headmaster is in.
headmasters_office.vibe: old wood, ink, green leaves, patient quiet.
headmasters_office.access: When it matters: discipline, requests, bad news

staff_quarters.name: Staff Quarters
staff_quarters.description: A separate stone house for the resident teaching staff (Dorm Heads live in their own dormitories instead), standing on its own beside the castle and joined to the castle's ground floor by a short covered walk: private rooms upstairs, and downstairs a shared parlour with mismatched armchairs, a kettle that is never cold, and a porch facing the Gardens. Where the Staff Room keeps students out, the Staff Quarters let them in: students may knock until the eight o'clock bell, and nothing said in the parlour counts as a consultation or a referral. It is where students come for help they would not ask for in class, advice about home, a second opinion on a club, or just tea with a teacher they like. Teachers here are off duty and act like it. Every door says something about who lives behind it: forest air draughting under Gavlan's, two teacups and a stack of theory on Layla's, and notes slid under Mimosa's, answered by morning. Vallie Goredust lives out by the Menagerie but holds court in the parlour anyway.

fire_dormitory.name: Fire Dormitory
fire_dormitory.description: Home of the Elementalists (red vest). Red-tiled roof and a red banner over the door. A great hearth burns in its common room day and night, and the broad chimney stack rising above the front of the building is always warm, even in winter. Inside: a common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Through the Elements, Victory Is Ours."
fire_dormitory.vibe: hearth warmth, a chimney warm even in winter, stone.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
lore.summary: Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.

seasons.Summer: The hearth burns anyway, and the common room is the hottest place on campus.
seasons.Winter: The hearth is the envy of the other three dormitories.

light_dormitory.name: Light Dormitory
light_dormitory.description: Home of the Mystics (yellow vest). Golden-tiled roof and a yellow banner over the door. Its inner court is roofed by a glass dome over the common area, which glows from within after dark. Inside: the glass dome common area plus personal rooms. Creed: "The Third Eye Lights The Way."

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
lore.summary: Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.

seasons.Summer: The dome turns the common area into a greenhouse by afternoon.
seasons.Winter: Snow slides off the warm glass dome, which glows brighter against the early dark.

sky_dormitory.name: Sky Dormitory
sky_dormitory.description:
Home of the Occultists (blue vest). Deep-blue-tiled roof and a blue banner over the door. A single slender tower rises from one corner, and the building's enchanted walls let residents see the academy grounds from their rooms; from outside the windows shimmer faintly, like water. Inside: common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Together We Are Strong."
Stigma: Occult carries a reputation no other type does. Outsiders associate it with blood magic, demon summoning, and spirits bound against their will, and cannot always tell legal Occult practice from forbidden work. The Doves watch Occultists more closely than any other dorm, and Sky students are often the first suspected when something goes wrong. The creed reflects this: Sky students close ranks because few others will stand with them.

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
lore.summary: Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.

viridian_dormitory.name: Viridian Dormitory
viridian_dormitory.description: Home of the Spiritualists (green vest). Green-tiled roof and a green banner over the door. An old oak fills its inner court, its crown rising above the roofline, with meditation stones set among its roots. Inside: common area, meditation rooms, personal rooms. Creed: "Know Thyself, Know Victory."

lore.title: Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
lore.summary: Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.

seasons.Spring: The inner oak comes into new leaf.
seasons.Summer: Deep shade over the meditation stones.
seasons.Autumn: The oak turns gold and leaves drift into the common area.
seasons.Winter: Bare branches over the roofline; the meditation stones sit under snow.

old_hut.name: Old Hut
old_hut.description: A one-room timber hut on the far slope of the Hills, where the grass runs out against the Forest treeline. Nobody remembers who built it or when; the Groundskeeper's Lodge lists it as disused and not worth repairing, and leaves it standing. The roof sags, the door hangs from one hinge, and the cold hearth still holds old ash. It is where students go to share secrets: far from every building and path, with nobody walking past, and by long student custom what is said inside the Old Hut stays there. Generations of confessions have left initials carved into the inside walls. It also serves as shelter from sudden rain, and on Star Night it is claimed before sunset. After dark nobody lingers, since it sits right on the Forest edge where patrols walk and names are not answered.
old_hut.vibe: weathered wood, wind through gaps, grass and pine.

seasons.Winter: Hardly anyone climbs to the Old Hut in winter: snow drifts against the door, the path over the Hills disappears, and a secret told there in the cold is one someone went to real trouble for.

announcement_room.name: Announcement Room
announcement_room.description: A small booth-like room off the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, home of the Academy Newspaper club. A speaking rune set into the desk carries whatever is said into it, live, to the Announcement Pillars around the grounds; nothing is recorded. Students on duty open the day with a good-morning after the seven o'clock bell and give the noon, afternoon and evening greetings, the last just before the eight o'clock bell. In between they read out what staff, the Student Council and event organisers send down, plus whatever the student on duty decides is important, the most argued-about power any club holds. Outside class periods the Music Club plays live from the side room, and the whole campus hears it. Staff can take over the rune for anything urgent; during The Thinning lockdown it is how the academy speaks to everyone at once.
announcement_room.vibe: cramped, warm lamplight, sheet music and newsprint.

broken_statue.name: Broken Statue
broken_statue.description: A white marble statue standing in a stand of old trees between the Fire Dormitory and the Dovecote, off the path students take when they would rather not walk past the Dovecote's front. The figure has lost its head and one arm; the arm lies half-sunk in the moss at its feet, and moss and lichen have crept over the rest until the white shows only in patches. The inscription on its plinth has worn smooth. Who it depicted is unknown, and nobody on staff claims to know; students have theories and none of them agree. Groundskeeping leaves it exactly as it is. Light comes through the leaves in pieces, and the place is quieter than it should be for somewhere so close to the courtyard.
broken_statue.vibe: green shade, cold marble, moss, stillness.

sparring_pavilion.name: The Sparring Pavilion
sparring_pavilion.description: A small round pavilion with a domed roof at the far corner of the Combat Grounds, the one building all four dorm training areas share. Inside: racks of training foci, ward-chalk and spare casting gear signed out by bracelet; benches, a water pump and a basic first-aid chest for the walk back after a hard session; a board of duel challenges and club standings. The club duels with spells inside warded rings, not staves. It is the Magic Duelling Club's headquarters, the standing exception to dorm separation, so it is the one place on the grounds where students of rival dorms share a bench. Gavlan Haverton, who advises the club, keeps a desk in the back. Unwritten rule: grudges from the rings are settled in the rings, never under the roof.
sparring_pavilion.vibe: sweat, strapped wrists, chalk dust, tired laughter.

fishing_house.name: Fishing House
fishing_house.description: The Fishing Club's timber hut on the lake shore, three minutes' walk along the shore from the boathouse, full of rods, nets and tackle, with its own long dock built for fishing rather than boats. Behind it, a stone-edged pond raises fish for the Canteen kitchen and the Fishing Club's breeding projects. The club meets here; the dock is busiest at dawn, and quiet enough that people come to sit on it without a rod.
fishing_house.vibe: tar, wet rope, early mist on the water.

seasons.Winter: A stove burns in the hut, and the dawn regulars fish from the end of the dock through the mist.

willow_island.name: Willow Island
willow_island.description: A small island in the middle of the lake with one great willow tree on it, reached only by a boat from the boathouse, which refuses bookings after dark. At night the willow glows in the distance from the many fireflies that live on the island, so anyone out there after dark was either rowed out before sunset or took a boat without asking.
willow_island.vibe: still water, trailing leaves, firefly light.
willow_island.access: By boat from the boathouse; no bookings after dark

seasons.Winter: The fireflies stay all winter, even over the ice, which Creature Studies cannot explain.

spirit_path.name: Spirit Path
spirit_path.description: A narrow footpath that leaves the grounds behind the Gymnasium and winds through old trees along the eastern edge of the academy, a loop short enough to walk in a quarter of an hour. Spirits like it here: the air under the trees is still and green, lesser spirits drift among the roots and branches, and small stone cairns that students have stacked over the years mark the way. Spirit users bring their pact partners here to let them out for a short walk. It is also where beginners come to meet a lesser spirit and try their first Spirit Pact; the custom is to go slowly, offer something small, and let the spirit choose. Almost any Occult student can bond a lesser spirit; a pact is a lasting contract, and the Occult teachers expect to be told of one. Anyone may come to watch: a stone bench at each bend faces the trees, and at dusk and dawn the lesser spirits are easy to see, a flicker in the ferns, a small light keeping pace along a branch. Most are shy; now and then one comes close out of curiosity, and it is considered lucky to be looked over and left in peace.
spirit_path.access: Open to students; unlit after dark, and curfew applies

seasons.Spring: Lesser spirits are thickest when the new leaves come; the path is busy with first-years.
seasons.Autumn: Fallen leaves stir on windless days. It is only the spirits.
seasons.Winter: Snow shows small tracks that stop in the middle of the path.

nightwell.name: Nightwell
nightwell.description:
A small Mall coffee house with one famous order, the Vigil.
Price: 60 points.
Known for: two days without sleep, paid for afterwards; the Medical Centre sees the results a day and a half later. Exam-week staple.

merryhews.name: Merryhew's
merryhews.description:
The Mall's joke shop: itching charms, voice-changing sweets, illusion vermin, screaming boxes, fake exam results convincing enough to be banned twice.
Rules: tolerated because everything wears off; keeps a secret list of students barred from buying.

snug.name: The Snug
snug.description:
A Mall eating house where every table is a partitioned private booth.
Known for: ordinary food, real privacy. Point loans, betting settlements, club trades, apologies and quiet negotiations; staff hear nothing. Booths by the hour, always a wait.

quillfeathers.name: Quillfeather's
quillfeathers.description: a narrow bookseller with a ladder on rails; new books at the front, second-hand at the back.

pennywhistle_curios.name: Pennywhistle Curios
pennywhistle_curios.description: gifts, games and trinkets; the window changes with every festival.

barrow_vine.name: Barrow & Vine
barrow_vine.description: wine, ale, spirits and tobacco. Asks for the bracelet, and reminds students they may drink only on the rest day and in the holidays.

greenwicks.name: Greenwick's
greenwicks.description: flowers, pot plants, seeds and fruit, run with the Gardening Club.

tinkers_bench.name: The Tinker's Bench
tinkers_bench.description: tools, craft and hobby supplies, fishing tackle and beast-care goods.

salaffian_oven.name: The Salaffian Oven
salaffian_oven.description: a food stall with flatbread straight from the oven and southern spices.

tailors_row.name: Tailor's Row
tailors_row.description: clothes, shoes, cologne and tailoring alterations.
